_about: Synthetic backlog (features -> stories -> tasks, acceptance criteria, architect requirements) written by Claude Code (AI), at the project owner's direction, against REAL merged pull requests in the seed snapshot. Tasks map to real commits by PR number or sha prefix. People here are fictional. Deliberate gaps: criteria with no linked code, criteria the linked code does not satisfy, requirements revised after the linked code merged, and commits that belong to no task. Requirements name their verification method; 'verifications' holds manual sign-offs (analysis, inspection, demonstration) tied to a specific build.

features.title: Pager and terminal output reliability
features.description: Paging, styling and progress output behave the same on every platform and honour the user's settings.

stories.title: Pager respects the user's PAGER and LESS settings

tasks.title: Forward PAGER parameters to the temp-file pager and parse less options
Close the pager temp file before unlinking it on Windows

criteria.text: When PAGER contains extra arguments (for example `less -R`), the temporary-file pager passes those arguments to the pager command instead of dropping them.
Raw-mode detection treats only real `-R`/`-r` short-option clusters or `--raw-control-chars` as a raw-mode request, not filenames or option values that happen to contain the letter r.
If an exception is raised while paging on Windows, the original exception is reported instead of a PermissionError from deleting the temporary file.
Paging a 50 MB output finishes in under 2 seconds on a typical laptop.

stories.title: Styled text renders correctly in prompts, wrapping and stripping

tasks.title: Strip ANSI codes from confirm() and prompt()
Strip the full CSI escape grammar

criteria.text: Help text wrapping measures line width in visible characters, so ANSI escape sequences don't count toward the width.
`confirm()` and `prompt()` remove colour codes from the prompt when the output stream doesn't support colour.
`unstyle()` removes colon-delimited true-colour sequences such as `\x1b[38:2:255:0:0m`.
`style()` raises an error for an invalid colour name, and the error message lists the valid colour names.
Passing `fg=0` to `style()` produces the 256-colour code for black instead of being silently ignored.

tasks.title: Settle the progress bar on its final position
Open the pager temp file in text mode

criteria.text: `click.edit()` accepts a `pathlib.Path`, or a list of paths, for `filename`.
The progress bar shows the full total (for example `20/20`) when it finishes, even if `update_min_steps` does not divide the length.
The user guide has a new section with an example of editing a `pathlib.Path` with `click.edit()`.
Writing a `str` to `get_pager_file()` works on Windows instead of raising TypeError.

features.title: Parameter API cleanup ahead of Click 9.0
features.description: Deprecate what 9.0 will remove, make help output complete and stable, and round out shell completion and testing helpers.

stories.title: Warn about parameter names Click 9.0 will reject

tasks.title: Add Parameter.spec and use it in messages
Write a codemod for renamed parameters

criteria.text: Declaring a parameter whose name is not a valid Python identifier, or is a Python keyword, emits a DeprecationWarning.
Error messages and deprecation warnings name an option the way the user types it (`--my-option`), not by its internal name (`my_option`).
`Parameter.human_readable_name` keeps working but emits a DeprecationWarning that points to `Parameter.spec`.
A codemod script renames deprecated parameter names in user projects automatically.

stories.title: Help output is complete and reproducible

tasks.title: Keep help option names in declaration order
Stop a parameter named help from breaking parsing

criteria.text: `Command.get_help_option_names` returns names in the order they were declared, so help output is identical across runs.
`@click.argument` accepts `help=`, and the help page shows a `Positional arguments` section when any argument has help.
A command with a parameter named `help` parses normally, and an argument that shares its name with another parameter triggers a warning.
Help output is translated into the user's locale when a translation catalogue is installed.

tasks.title: Ship a PowerShell completion source script

criteria.text: Setting `_FOO_BAR_COMPLETE=powershell_source` prints a completion script that registers an argument completer for the program.
The shell completion docs list PowerShell alongside bash, zsh and fish, with setup instructions for the PowerShell profile.
PowerShell completion is verified by an automated test that runs a real `pwsh` process in CI.
Completion responds within 100 ms for a CLI with 500 subcommands.

tasks.title: Add a file-descriptor capture mode to CliRunner
Deprecate isolated_filesystem and document the replacement

criteria.text: `CliRunner` accepts `capture='fd'`, which also captures output written straight to file descriptors 1 and 2.
`CliRunner.isolated_filesystem()` emits a DeprecationWarning, and the testing docs show the temporary-directory replacement.
`capture='fd'` works on Windows.

features.title: Robust request body and header handling
features.description: Accept every reasonable file-like object, and parse URLs and headers defensively.

stories.title: Accept file-like wrappers that proxy attributes

tasks.title: Detect streams through hasattr in prepare_body

criteria.text: Request bodies that wrap a file through `__getattr__` (without defining `__iter__` themselves) are streamed instead of rejected.
Multipart uploads accept file objects that only expose `read` through `__getattr__`.
All read-capability checks go through one helper function instead of repeated isinstance checks.
The change is recorded in the HISTORY changelog for the next release.

tasks.title: Anchor header validity regexes at end of string
Stop responses referencing themselves in redirect history

criteria.text: Header names and values that end in a newline (`\n` or `\r\n`) are rejected as invalid.
A Content-Type header whose parameter has no `=` (for example `text/html; charset`) falls back to the default encoding instead of producing a bogus charset.
Request URLs whose path starts with `//` keep both slashes when sent.
After following redirects, no response in `history` contains itself in its own `history`.
Invalid headers are logged at WARNING level, with the header name, before the request is rejected.

features.title: Inline type annotations
features.description: Ship accurate inline types so users get editor help and type checking without a stubs package.

stories.title: Ship inline types with the package

tasks.title: Add inline types and a type-check workflow

criteria.text: `Request.hooks` has a type annotation.
CI runs a type checker on every pull request.
The package passes Pyright in strict mode with zero errors.

stories.title: Header and response types match runtime behaviour

tasks.title: Make Request.headers a read-only Mapping again

criteria.text: `Request.headers` is typed as a read-only `Mapping[str, str | bytes]`.
`Response.reason` is typed as `str`.
A runtime check raises `TypeError` when headers are passed as a list of tuples.

tasks.title: Mark DigestAuth hashes as not used for security
Fix no_proxy matching for leading-dot entries
Publish a security advisory for the no_proxy fix

criteria.text: DigestAuth works on FIPS-enabled systems by passing `usedforsecurity=False` to every hashlib call it makes.
`no_proxy` entries with a leading dot (for example `.example.com`) match the domain itself as well as its subdomains.
DigestAuth supports the SHA-512-256 algorithm.
A security advisory is published for the no_proxy fix.

features.title: Simpler TLS and proxy configuration (0.28)
features.description: One obvious way to configure TLS, clear errors for old patterns, and better proxy support.

tasks.title: Raise a helpful error for verify=<str>

criteria.text: `verify` accepts `True`, `False` or an `ssl.SSLContext`, and the separate `ssl_context` parameter is removed.
Passing a string to `verify` raises an error that tells the user to use `ssl.create_default_context(cafile=...)` instead.
Passing a string to `verify` raises `TypeError`.
Importing httpx does not import the `ssl` module until a client actually needs it.
Using `verify=False` together with a client certificate (`cert=...`) still loads the certificate instead of ignoring it.
The documentation describes the `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `SSL_CERT_DIR` environment variables.

tasks.title: Show the proxy scheme in the error

criteria.text: `socks5h://` proxy URLs are accepted and routed through the SOCKS transport.
The error for an unsupported proxy scheme includes the scheme the user passed.
Proxy credentials (user and password in the proxy URL) are never written to log output.

features.title: URL handling and internal cleanup
features.description: Encode URLs the way browsers do and pay down internal module debt.

tasks.title: Use default safe characters for urlescape

criteria.text: Query parameters encode spaces as `+` (form encoding).
A `/` inside a query parameter value is percent-encoded as `%2F`.
The behaviour change is called out in the CHANGELOG under backwards-incompatible changes.
The redirect helpers (`same_origin`, `is_https_redirect`) live in `_client.py` as private functions, and their tests moved next to the client tests.
`httpx/_utils.py` is deleted.
A response with `Content-Encoding: zstd` and an empty body decodes to empty bytes instead of raising.
A truncated zstd body raises `httpx.DecodingError`.
Brotli decoding handles empty bodies the same way.

requirements.title: Third-party client libraries meet the platform dependency baseline
requirements.author: arjun-patel

revisions.body: Every third-party library the platform ships must meet the dependency baseline: predictable terminal output, standards-compliant HTTP behaviour, and no credential leakage. Verified when every subsystem requirement below it is verified.

requirements.title: Command-line output library (click) meets the baseline
requirements.author: arjun-patel

revisions.body: The command-line library behaves predictably in user terminals and announces breaking changes. Verified by its component requirements.

requirements.title: HTTP client libraries (requests, httpx) meet the baseline
requirements.author: arjun-patel

revisions.body: The HTTP client libraries accept common inputs, configure TLS and encode URLs predictably, and never leak credentials. Verified by its component requirements.
Click must honour the user's PAGER setting, including any arguments it carries, on every platform.

Click must honour the user's PAGER setting, including any arguments it carries, on every platform. On Windows the temporary-file pager must also honour options set in the LESS environment variable and write with the stream's encoding.
revisions.note: Added LESS handling and encoding after a customer report.

revisions.body: Any styled text Click produces or receives must render correctly on colour terminals and be cleanly stripped where colour isn't supported.

requirements.title: Breaking changes are announced one minor release ahead
requirements.author: arjun-patel

revisions.body: Anything Click 9.0 removes must emit a DeprecationWarning in 8.x and be listed in the upgrade guide.

requirements.title: Anything that behaves like a file is accepted
requirements.author: arjun-patel

revisions.body: Requests must accept any object that provides the file methods it needs, whether defined directly or proxied through __getattr__.

requirements.title: Public type hints describe what callers may pass
requirements.author: arjun-patel

revisions.body: Header inputs accept mutable mappings so callers can pass dict or CaseInsensitiveDict.
Header inputs are typed as read-only Mapping: Requests never mutates a caller's headers.

Header inputs are typed as read-only Mapping: Requests never mutates a caller's headers. Response and Request attributes, including hooks, carry precise types with no Optional where the runtime never yields None.
revisions.note: Extended to attributes after the 2.33 typing review.

revisions.body: No hashing call may fail on a FIPS-enabled interpreter.

requirements.title: TLS configuration has one obvious way
requirements.author: arjun-patel

revisions.body: TLS is configured through verify (bool or ssl.SSLContext) only. Old string forms fail with a message that shows the replacement.
TLS is configured through verify (bool or ssl.SSLContext) only. Old string forms raise TypeError with a message that shows the replacement.
revisions.note: Error type tightened to TypeError to match Python conventions for a wrong argument type.

requirements.title: URLs are encoded the way browsers encode them
requirements.author: arjun-patel

revisions.body: Percent-encoding follows the WHATWG URL standard.
Credentials in URLs, headers or proxy settings are masked before anything is logged.
